summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload at npm install
details: @onereach/si-dropdown-simple@0.4.7 is published as a Vue dropdown component but ships an install-time dropper. Its package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-mangled dictionary indirection over execFileSync, https.get, fs.writeFileSync, chmodSync) and, at npm install time, downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (URL constructed as `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<V>/<arch>.zip`), unpacks it into a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync to run the adjacent math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB obfuscator.io-style bundle (marked `// @bun @bun-cjs`, rotated string array, control-flow-flattened dispatcher) whose behavior cannot be reviewed as source. The file name and contents bear no relationship to a Vue dropdown component. Fetching a foreign language runtime specifically to execute an opaque bundle at install time is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern used to evade Node-based scanners, and the preinstall hook causes it to fire automatically on default `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
